newsitem.title: USA: Gingrich expects positive role if Democrats win.
newsitem.headline: Gingrich expects positive role if Democrats win.

text.p: Whichever party wins control of Congress next Tuesday, House Speaker Newt Gingrich says repeated personal attacks by Democrats have guaranteed that he will not disappear from the political landscape.

The Georgia Republican, who recently has been besieged by speculation about his own future, put the odds of a Republican victory in the House and his own return to the chamber's helm at more than 90 percent.
But even if the House careers into Democratic territory on Nov. 5, Gingrich told Reuters in an interview that he would not go gently into the night of political obscurity.

"I am the only House member ever to have 75,000 commercials run against him. That's the current number," Gingrich said, recounting a national Democratic campaign to make him the poster boy for unpopular Republican policies.
"The Dole media purchase person pulled it up last night and was astonished. He called me and said: 'I just want you to know the Democrats have now used you in 75,000 commercials'.
"We may break 95,000 by the time we get to the election. So in that sense, they've built my name ID," he quipped.

Gingrich, 53, a main architect of the so-called Republican revolution, last week took the rare step of refuting a conservative Boston Globe columnist's report that he had told fund-raisers he would resign rather than face a House ethics investigations in the hands of Democrats.
In a written statement denying the "ridiculous assertion," the speaker said he would relinquish party leadership in the event of a Democratic victory but would remain in Congress.
The speaker, who also is seeking re-election this year, has been widely expected to defeat Democratic challenger Michael Coles in Georgia's 6th Congressional District race.

On Wednesday Gingrich said he would step back from the task of fighting a Democratic majority. But he would take on "positive" high-profile Republican projects, including a programme to educate the public about diabetes, which he said represents 27 percent of all Medicare costs.

"The Democrats, if they get to be in charge, will be so bad. Between covering up Clinton's scandals and trying to pass the kind of left-wing legislation that they did in '93-'94, you need somebody who's going to be very enthusiastically fighting them every single day," he said.
"I'd want to focus on communicating our positive vision of the future, and on solving problems."
Asked if he would remain leader of the conservative wing of the Republican party, Gingrich reverted to expectations for a clear election victory next week.
"I don't worry about it much. The odds are literally nine to one, or better, that I'll be speaker," he said.
